advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the host-script scan call `_runs_without_init` instead of repeating the `--init` regex inline.
evidence:
def _runs_without_init(script: str) -> list[str]:
    return [run for run in _detached_runs(script) if not re.search(r"\s--init\b", run)]
if (bad := [r for r in found if not re.search(r"\s--init\b", r)])
assert _runs_without_init(seeded) == [ ... ]  (the seeded test exercises the helper, not the inline copy)
advisory.finding: The real check `test_every_detached_docker_run_in_the_host_scripts_runs_an_init` writes out its own `--init` regex instead of calling `_runs_without_init`. The seeded test checks `_runs_without_init`, which the real check never calls, so the two can drift apart without either test failing.
scenarios: Someone changes the regex in `_runs_without_init` (for example, to accept `--init=true`). The seeded test passes, but the real scan still uses the old inline regex.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the inline comprehension with `missing = {name: bad for name, text in scripts.items() if (bad := _runs_without_init(text))}`, reading each script once.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the detached-run detector match bundled short flags that contain `d` (for example `-itd` and `-dit`).
evidence: if re.search(r"\bdocker run\b", line) and re.search(r"\s(-d|--detach)\b", line)
For `-itd`, the `\s-` must be followed directly by `d`, but it is followed by `i`. For `-dit`, `\b` fails between `d` and `i`. Either way the line is never treated as detached.
advisory.finding: `_detached_runs` only treats a `docker run` as detached when it sees a standalone `-d` or `--detach`. A bundled short flag such as `docker run -itd ...` or `-dit` does not match, so the guard silently skips that container instead of flagging the missing `--init`.
scenarios: A future host script adds `docker run -itd --name x img` without `--init`. The guard passes, and the container runs its server as PID 1 again.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `re.search(r"\s(--detach\b|-[A-Za-z]*d[A-Za-z]*\b)", line)` and add a `-itd` case to the seeded test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update docs/concurrency.md and the PID-1 docstrings to say docker-init is PID 1 and forwards SIGTERM to the server.
evidence: docs/concurrency.md:496-497: "The detached worker runs in its own session, so a container stop signal sent to the MCP server (PID 1) never reaches it."
tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:555-558: "Backgrounding must not have cost us PID-1 semantics. ... the server replaces the shell and receives SIGTERM directly"
tests/unit/test_mcp_retire_sweep.py:3: "``docker stop`` signals only the container's PID 1 (the MCP server)"
advisory.finding: The change makes docker-init PID 1, but existing docs and test docstrings still say the MCP server is PID 1 and receives SIGTERM directly.
scenarios: An operator debugging stop or drain behaviour reads concurrency.md and expects the server to be PID 1. It is actually tini, which forwards signals only to its direct child.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the entrypoint source regex with a subprocess test: run the default startup path with stubbed provisioning and an exec target that reports its own children, and assert there are none.
evidence: tests/unit/test_container_init_reaper.py: `body = _ENTRYPOINT.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` then `assert re.search(r"^\(\s*provision_store\s*&\s*\)\s*$", body, re.MULTILINE)`
The regex is anchored at `\s*$`, so a behavior-identical `( provision_store & )  # detach` fails it. So does moving the call into a helper such as `start_provisioning() { ( provision_store & ); }`.
The negative check `^provision_store\s*&\s*$` is anchored at column 0, so an indented `  provision_store &` reintroduced in a branch is not caught.
infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:387-388: `( provision_store & )` / `exec "$@"`. The behavior is observable by running the script with an exec target that lists its own children.
tests/unit/test_mcp_entrypoint_provisioning.py:226-233 already runs `sh <entrypoint>` in a subprocess with stubbed git/ensure scripts, so a behavioral harness exists.
advisory.finding: The entrypoint guard matches a regex against the shell script's source instead of running it. It checks the text `( provision_store & )`, not the behavior that the exec'd server has no unwaited provisioning child. So it fails on refactors that keep the behavior, and it would pass if the line were present but never ran.
scenarios: A maintainer adds a trailing comment or extracts the detach into a helper function. The test goes red even though reaping is unchanged.
The detach line stays but is unreachable on the default startup path. The test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reuse the stub environment from test_mcp_entrypoint_provisioning.py. Run `sh mcp-entrypoint.sh sh -c 'sleep 0.3; ps -o pid= --ppid $$'` with a provisioning stub that sleeps. Assert returncode 0 and empty stdout. With the old `provision_store &` the provisioning shell would be listed as a child of the exec'd process.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `assert "--init" in run_line` (tied to compose mcp `init: true`) to the compose-parity test in tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py instead of relying on the source grep.
evidence: tests/unit/test_container_init_reaper.py: `found = _detached_runs(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))`. This is a text scan of executable shell source.

`_detached_runs` requires `re.search(r"\s(-d|--detach)\b", line)`, so `docker run -dit ...` (no word boundary after `-d`) or a `"$DOCKER" run -d` wrapper would not count as detached. A missing `--init` in those forms would pass silently.

tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:1318-1329 already asserts `"--restart always" in run_line`, `"--stop-timeout 1260" in run_line` and `f"--memory {mem_limit}" in run_line` on the captured docker-stub argv. There is no matching `--init` assertion.
advisory.finding: The `--init` guard for the blue-green MCP container greps autodeploy.sh's text instead of the `docker run` command line that autodeploy actually builds. The repo already has a compose-parity test that captures that command line and asserts each compose-mirrored flag. It was not extended to check that compose `init: true` maps to `--init`.
scenarios: The run is rewritten as `docker run -dit --name "$1" ...` without `--init`. `_detached_runs` skips it and the guard passes.
The flag is built into an argv array or variable, e.g. `opts+=(--init)`, and spliced in. The text scan cannot see it even though the executed command carries it.
advisory.suggested_fix: In tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py next to the `--restart always` assertion (~line 1318), add: `assert "--init" in run_line, f"docker run must pass --init to mirror compose mcp init: true\n{ctx}"`.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the exact service-set pin with a non-empty/minimum check (e.g. assert `{"review-bot", "mcp"} <= set(_services())`), or drop it.
evidence: tests/unit/test_container_init_reaper.py: `_SERVICES = {"gerrit", "review-bot", "opcert", "mcp"}` and `assert set(_services()) == _SERVICES`
`_services_without_init` checks every entry: `sorted(name for name, svc in services.items() if svc.get("init") is not True)`. A new service is never silently skipped.
dropped.finding: `test_the_guard_covers_exactly_the_compose_services` pins the exact set of compose service names. It adds no detection, because `_services_without_init` already checks every service in the file, so a new service without `init` already fails. It only goes red when a service is added or renamed, even with `init: true` set.
scenarios: A fifth compose service is added with `init: true`. This test fails with no reaping regression.
dropped.suggested_fix: Replace `assert set(_services()) == _SERVICES` with `assert _SERVICES <= set(_services())`. This keeps the anti-vacuity guarantee and stops failing when a service is added.

dropped.finding: docs/concurrency.md still says a container stop signal is "sent to the MCP server (PID 1)". The change makes docker-init (tini) PID 1 in the MCP container, and the server now runs as tini's child. The maintained concurrency model therefore misstates the MCP container's process structure and signal path.
scenarios: A contributor investigating MCP shutdown or sweep-worker signaling reads docs/concurrency.md and assumes the server receives `docker stop` directly as PID 1, missing that tini receives the signal and forwards it to the server.
dropped.suggested_fix: In docs/concurrency.md line 496-497, replace "a container stop signal sent to the MCP server (PID 1) never reaches it" with wording such as "a container stop signal, which the container's init (PID 1) forwards to the MCP server, never reaches it".
